 ▶ Janice Tjen defeats Robin Montgomery at Chennai Open 2026 – Semi-Final 
 1217 views • 1d Janice Tjen reached the Chennai Open final with a 6-3, 6-4 victory over Robin Montgomery in 1 hour 23 minutes. The No. 75-ranked Indonesian controlled a hard-court semifinal against the No. 151 American and closed out a significant progression opportunity.
The result extended Tjen’s current winning streak to four matches. She also overcame Polina Kudermetova in a three-set quarterfinal and has now won 11 of her last 22 recorded hard-court matches, including victories over players ranked No. 93, No. 196 and No. 151 in Chennai.
Tjen’s overall record across the supplied 40-match sample is 17 wins and 23 losses, but her recent results show a clear improvement. Before this run, she had lost to Harriet Dart, Ashlyn Krueger and Ann Li, while also recording notable hard-court wins over Daria Snigur and Anhelina Kalinina.
Montgomery arrived in the semifinal with three straight Chennai victories, including a 6-4, 1-6, 6-1 win over No. 86 Panna Udvardy and a 6-4, 3-6, 7-5 battle against No. 126 Jeline Vandromme. Her last 40 matches show a 26-14 record, although the loss ended her latest hard-court run.
The ranking gap made Tjen the higher-positioned player, and her ability to finish the match in straight sets prevented Montgomery from extending another contest into a deciding set.
